title: Secondary Storage and Device Choice
intro: A short, self-paced catch-up covering the essential lesson ideas. Check every question, then correct anything missed.

stages.label: Remember
stages.lead: Recall two useful ideas from earlier lessons.

questions.prompt: What does RAM store during execution?
options: Active program instructions and working data
questions.answer: Active program instructions and working data
questions.feedback: RAM supplies fast volatile working storage.

questions.prompt: A mono recording uses 2,000 samples per second for 3 seconds at 8 bits per sample. How many raw bytes?

stages.label: Learn
stages.lead: Read the essential ideas and worked example before checking your understanding.

blocks.title: Non-volatile storage
blocks.text: Secondary storage keeps saved files and programs without power.

blocks.title: Three technologies
blocks.text: Magnetic HDDs use magnetic patterns; optical discs use lasers; solid-state memory uses chips with no moving mechanical parts.

blocks.title: Comparison
blocks.text: Consider capacity, read/write speed, portability, durability, reliability and cost.

blocks.title: Justification
blocks.text: Link a stated feature of a device to the actual user requirement; no technology is always the best choice.

blocks.title: Visual model · Secondary Storage and Device Choice
blocks.caption: Compare speed, capacity, price per GB, portability, reliability and physical durability.

blocks.title: Worked model · A travelling photographer needs to move large files quickly and often drops their bag. Choose a storage device.
blocks.text: Identify speed, portability and physical durability as priorities. Recommend a portable SSD. Explain that an SSD usually transfers large files quickly. Explain why its lack of moving mechanical parts reduces risk of knock damage. Mention that SSDs can cost more per GB than HDDs and backups are still needed.

items: magnetic — Uses magnetic properties to record bits.
optical — Uses laser light to read disc data.
solid-state — Uses memory chips without moving read/write heads.
secondary storage — Non-volatile storage for saved files and programs.

questions.prompt: Which storage technology uses spinning magnetic platters?
questions.feedback: Hard disk drives store information magnetically on rotating platters.

questions.prompt: Which storage uses a laser to read a disc?
questions.feedback: CDs and DVDs use optical laser read/write technology.

questions.prompt: Which choice is most resistant to shocks because it has no moving read/write heads?
questions.feedback: Solid-state storage uses memory chips rather than mechanical read/write heads.

stages.label: Practise
stages.lead: Match, reorder and apply what you have learnt.

blocks.text: A good recommendation starts with the user requirement, not a brand or specification.

questions.prompt: Match the storage type to the technology.
questions.feedback: Storage devices rely on different physical methods.

questions.prompt: Put a sensible storage recommendation process in order.
items: Justify the selected device using those priorities
answer: Justify the selected device using those priorities
questions.feedback: A valid justification links features to the actual requirement.

questions.prompt: Which is often economical per GB for a very large school archive?
questions.feedback: HDDs often provide large capacity at lower cost per GB.

questions.prompt: What does non-volatile secondary storage mean?
options: Data remains after power is switched off
Data is stored only in CPU registers
Every file is kept in cache
questions.answer: Data remains after power is switched off
questions.feedback: Saved data persists without a continuous power supply.
